headline: Just Been Arrested on State Charges? Here's What to Know

publisher.name: Law Office of Angelo J. Reyes, APC

articleBody: An arrest on state criminal charges can throw your life into disarray, leaving you confused and anxious about what comes next. It’s a stressful time, but knowing what to do immediately after an arrest can significantly impact your case's outcome. First, remember your right to remain silent. You are not obligated to answer questions from law enforcement without an attorney present. Politely but firmly state that you wish to speak with a lawyer before answering anything. Anything you say can be used against you, so it's always best to keep quiet. Secondly, don't resist arrest, even if you believe it's unlawful. Resisting can lead to additional charges and can escalate the situation unnecessarily. Cooperate physically, but mentally invoke your right to silence. Thirdly, ask to make a phone call as soon as you're able. Use this call to contact a trusted family member or, ideally, directly call an experienced state criminal defense lawyer. The sooner legal representation is secured, the faster they can begin protecting your rights, advising you on your next steps, and investigating your case. Don't try to navigate the complex state legal system alone. An attorney can help you understand the charges, explore defense strategies, and represent you effectively at every stage, from arraignment to trial.
